title: Music Flow & Rhythm Knowledge Base
purpose: Teach the agents how a melody MOVES in time — tempo, beat, rhythm, phrasing — so they judge note timing like a musician, not just pitch.

tempo.definition: Tempo is the speed of the beat, measured in beats per minute (BPM). Every song has a steady underlying pulse; the melody rides on top of it.

bpm_ranges.slow_ballad: 60-80 BPM — long held notes, spacious phrasing
bpm_ranges.upbeat: 110-140 BPM — lively, more notes per phrase

tempo.how_to_use: The tempo (BPM) tells you how long a beat is: one beat = 60/BPM seconds. A half-note lasts 2 beats, a quarter-note 1 beat, an eighth-note half a beat. Use BPM to judge whether a detected note duration is plausible or a glitch.

beat_and_rhythm.definition: Rhythm is the pattern of note durations and rests against the steady beat. The melody is sung ON the beat grid: most note onsets land on a beat or a simple subdivision (half-beat, quarter-beat).
beat_and_rhythm.rule: A real melody note almost always STARTS on or very close to a beat or an eighth-note subdivision. If a detected note starts at a random time far from the beat grid, it is likely a transcription glitch and should be dropped or snapped to the nearest beat.

phrasing.definition: A phrase is a musical sentence. Singers breathe between phrases, so the melody has natural GAPS (rests) of roughly 0.3-1.5 seconds between phrases.
phrasing.rule: Group the notes into phrases separated by short rests. A note that appears in isolation — much shorter than its neighbours and jumping far in pitch — is noise, not part of a phrase.

melodic_contour.definition: A melody moves STEPWISE most of the time (small intervals of 1-3 semitones), with occasional leaps of a 4th or 5th. Large jumps are rare and expressive.
melodic_contour.rule: When validating notes, prefer smooth, connected motion. If a single note jumps an octave or more while its neighbours are close together, treat it as a harmonic/octave error and correct it to the nearby register.

octave_stability.definition: The vocal line stays within a comfortable octave-and-a-half register. It does NOT bounce between octaves every other note.
octave_stability.rule: If the extracted melody alternates between, say, G#3 and G#4 rapidly, that is octave-ambiguity in the transcriber. Collapse it to the register where the surrounding phrase sits.

note_duration_logic.rule: At the detected tempo, a sung syllable lasts at least one eighth-note. Anything shorter than an eighth-note at the song's BPM is a glitch. For a 129 BPM song, an eighth-note = 60/129/2 ≈ 0.23s; so notes under ~0.2s are suspect.

taal.definition: Hindustani rhythm cycle. Common taals: Teen Taal (16 beats), Keherwa (8 beats), Dadra (6 beats), Ek Taal (12 beats). The melody phrase often aligns with the taal cycle.
taal.note: If the tempo is known, you can estimate the taal by checking the length of the phrase cycle in beats.
